conceptZh: 一臉嚴肅的玩具機器人裁判努力板著臉，旁邊小企鵝玩具在平地上莫名其妙滑倒、四腳朝天；裁判的面板憋到裂出一道笑紋，最後整個抖起來無聲大笑，帽子都掉了。
object: a stern toy robot referee and a tiny cartoon penguin
morph: the glyph 笑 stands still as a solid sculpture while the trying-not-to-laugh gag plays out beside it
creativeAngle: 直接對上孩子喜歡的搞笑：用「憋笑失敗」這個大人小孩都懂的身體笑話演字義，跟忍字的憋噴嚏不同在於這次是憋不住、整個爆開。笑上為竹部下為夭，竹已經學過可以互相連結。語音詞「大笑」，大在此念ㄉㄚˋ、笑念ㄒㄧㄠˋ，都是課本讀音，不會念成ㄉㄞˋ。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale mint background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 笑 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep magenta, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the 竹 radical on top, its two halves evenly matched, sits above the 夭 component with its sweeping left stroke and long right stroke clearly separated. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. Beside its lower right stands a stern toy robot referee with a flat visor face, a tiny whistle and an even tinier cap, arms folded, absolutely determined to stay serious. From 0.7 seconds a tiny cartoon penguin waddles across the bottom of frame on perfectly flat, perfectly empty ground - and slips anyway, feet flying up, landing softly on its back with its flippers sticking straight up. It stays exactly like that. The referee's visor stays rigid. Beat. At 2.3 seconds a single crack of a grin appears at the corner of his visor; he clamps it flat again and stiffens his arms. At 3.0 seconds the penguin waggles one flipper. The referee loses it completely: from 3.2 to 4.3 seconds his whole body shakes with silent laughter, his visor curving into an enormous grin, his tiny cap bouncing off his head and landing on the penguin's tummy. By 4.7 seconds both of them have wobbled happily out of frame to the right. From 4.8 to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 笑 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「笑、笑、大笑」, using the reading ㄒㄧㄠˋ for 笑 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 笑 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 大笑 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 笑: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 科學家老鼠想吹平冒泡的實驗液，卻吹出一副比自己還寬的泡泡鬍子；鬍子搔到鼻尖，牠忍不住笑開了。
object: A meticulous, bespectacled cartoon lab mouse with one molded twin-chamber bubbling beaker
morph: The complete glyph remains intact while an oversized foam moustache makes the mouse demonstrate laughter beside it.
creativeAngle: 改用老鼠親自操作失手的泡泡實驗：越想吹平泡沫，鬍子反而越大，最後被自己的鬍子逗笑。以動作呈現「笑」的意思，字形全程完整，避免道具變筆畫造成誤讀。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation in one locked, front-facing shot. On a pale peach background, place the single Traditional Chinese glyph 笑 precisely at frame center, uncropped and approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Render its strokes in solid saturated raspberry, using a correctly formed standard Taiwanese textbook glyph: the clear 竹 radical above 夭, with every stroke and internal gap preserved. Keep this glyph fully visible, stationary and unchanged throughout. All characters and objects are original animated designs, with rounded toy-like materials and soft studio lighting.

In the open lower-left margin, stage a small, bespectacled cartoon scientist mouse with oversized round ears, a molded lavender laboratory coat and an enthusiastically meticulous personality. Its sole separate prop is one molded twin-chamber beaker, both chambers visibly bubbling with pastel liquid. Keep the entire gag outside the glyph’s silhouette, with enough room to read the mouse’s expressions.

At 0.0–1.4 seconds, the mouse scrutinizes the rising foam, proudly straightens its spectacles, then carefully blows across the beaker to flatten the bubbles. Pause briefly as the foam seems to settle. At 1.4–2.7 seconds, the chambers gently fizz over together: two connected curls of foam rise onto its upper lip, making an absurdly wide, curled moustache. The mouse goes cross-eyed at it and gives one determined little puff; the moustache balloons even wider. At 2.7–4.0 seconds, its curled tips bend inward and tickle the mouse’s nose. The mouse scrunches its face, then breaks into unmistakable silent laughter, eyes squeezed into happy crescents and belly bouncing. The foam collapses into the beaker with a soft plop. At 4.0–4.6 seconds, the mouse beams at the now-settled liquid, proudly hugs its successful experiment and scampers off the left edge with the beaker. From 4.6–8.0 seconds, hold completely still on the clean, centered 笑 alone for 3.4 full seconds.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「笑、笑、笑臉」. Pronounce 笑 as ㄒㄧㄠˋ each time, including within 笑臉. Place the first 笑 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 3.0 seconds, and 笑臉 around 5.6 seconds during the unobstructed final hold. Use natural pauses and stop after the word. The mouse’s laughter is visual only; keep bubbling and the foam plop soft beneath the narration, with no music. Only 笑 appears as writing anywhere in the image; the vocabulary stays audio only. Maintain a bright, uncluttered composition without subtitles, labels, logos, watermarks, flashing effects or blown-out highlights.
